title: Immunoblot Analysis for Immunodetection of HIV Proteins
author: Angel A Justiz-Vaillant
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bjtpknmn

steps.title: Prepare SDS-PAGE running buffer
steps.instruction: Make running buffer containing 25 mM Tris, 192 mM glycine (pH 8.3), and 20 % (v/v) methanol.

steps.title: Load serum and run SDS-PAGE
steps.instruction: Aliquot 3–5 µL of each serum sample onto the gel and run the SDS‑PAGE using the prepared running buffer.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to nitrocellulose membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer the resolved gels onto Immobilon‑NC nitrocellulose membranes (pore size 0.45 µm) with a semi‑dry electroblotter (HEP‑1 Model, Owl Scientific Inc) for 75 min at 40 mA.

steps.title: Block membrane and wash
steps.instruction: Incubate membranes overnight in blocking solution of 10 % non‑fat skim milk in PBS containing 0.05 % Tween‑20 (pH 7.4). Then wash membranes four times, each wash for 10 min, with PBS‑Tween‑20.

steps.title: Incubate with peroxidase‑anti‑HIV conjugate
steps.instruction: Add peroxidase‑labeled anti‑HIV conjugate to the blocked membranes and incubate at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Wash and develop immunoblot
steps.instruction: Wash the membranes as above (four 10‑min washes with PBS‑Tween‑20), then add tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) substrate, allow color development, and stop the reaction by rinsing with deionised water.
